dating: Most current: W17 (May 2025) and the service yard W1-W4 (2019/2025). The south face (W9-W15) is Aug 2015 and W8/W14/W16 Sep 2014; Earth 2024 thumbnails agree on massing, window bands and colours, so nothing major seems to have changed, but W8's boarded openings and the 2014 ground signs may be different now. Earth over-pinks the brick.

W0.summary: north end: two volumes. s 0-17.6 is the brick east block (6.9 m) wrapping round from W17 with the same deep dark fascia and clerestory strip, a steel door near the NE corner with ONE WAY / YIELD signs; s 17.6-39.1 is a windowless grey concrete-block wall, 7.3-7.7 m, with LED wall packs
attached: block part: LED wall packs at about s 28 and 38, z 4.3; control joints every ~6.8 m
W0.notes: Brick/block boundary at s ~17.6 from sv_W0_Nlip (2019, 4 m away, clerestory windows visible at the top of the brick part); s 25-39 all block in sv_c20 and sv_W0_tFyc. The door and signs are on the NE return in sv_W0_kgy5 (2014). The clerestory strip extent on the brick part (s 6-17) is a guess from the cut-off windows in Nlip and the 2014 view. Earth (W0 whole, c19) shows a sloping slab-like thing in front of s ~10-20 that the lidar does not have (0 m out to 5 m) - probably a mesh artefact or a thin canopy; not modelled.

W1.summary: east side of the service yard: 7.8 m windowless grey block with numbered doors 1-5: a brown overhead door and a steel man door at dock height (1.2 m, steel stair), a tall dark-green sectional door, a dock door with bumpers and a drive-in door under a short dark steel canopy
attached: steel stair with pipe railing up to door 2's dock-height landing, s 3.2-6.0, 1.8 m out
black rubber dock bumpers under doors 1 and 4
single dark steel canopy over doors 4 and 5, s 16.1-25.9, z 4.4-5.0, ~1.5 m deep (two door canopies approximate it)
wall packs at s 5.5 and 20 (z 3.5)
black 'Do Not Enter' sign at the a corner
W1.notes: Positions from sv_W1_v3zs (whole wall, 2019) and sv_W1_ExAo close-up. Doors 1-2 sit at dock height 1.2 m; door 3 starts ~0.3 m. The 'brick part with door 6' seen at the right of v3zs belongs to W2.

W2.summary: two-storey brick block at the yard's SE inner corner (8.2 m): three windows upstairs, a grey metal duct riser running up the face and over the roof, the PLANT OPERATIONS door 6 and a white-framed window at ground; the west 2/3 of the ground floor is grey block under the dark loading canopy
attached: loading canopy (projecting band) 2.7 m deep at z 4.2-4.8 along the whole wall, continuing west as W3; dark steel posts with yellow-painted bases at its edge ~2.5 m apart, s 5-15
grey metal duct riser s 3.5-5.0 from z 5.6 to 9.6 (1.4 m above the roof)
dark metal corner panel s 14.4-15.3 full height
small wall-mounted exhaust fan cowl at s ~1, z 3.5
W2.notes: From sv_W2_ExAo and sv_c23 (2019). Lidar has the 4.8 m canopy 0-2.5 m in front of the whole wall. Window/door positions scaled from the 14.4 m brick width; +-0.5 m.

W3.summary: the long loading dock on the yard's south side: this line is the edge of a dark steel canopy (fascia z 4.2-4.9); the grey block wall stands 2.9 m behind it with numbered doors 7-12: glazed staff door, steel doors, two open dock openings with man doors, a brown overhead door
attached: canopy soffit: exposed dark steel beams ~2.2 m apart; posts only at the east end (s 0-3, continuing along W2), cantilevered over the truck docks further west
wall packs over doors 7, 9, 12
small white instruction plates beside doors
W3.notes: Lidar: roof 4.9 m right up to this line and 0 m 1 m outside, while photos show the doors well behind the fascia; W3 starts 2.9 m in front of W2's line, so the wall is on W2's line and the canopy is ~2.9 m deep. Door positions merged from sv_W3_v3zs, sv_W3_XcRP, sv_c23 (2019), perspective error +-2 m. Doors 9 and 12 were open (dark interior) in every photo.

W4.summary: vehicle-maintenance garage on the yard's west side: grey block with six numbered drive-in bays 15-20 (2.9 m wide, 3.6 m high), dark brown metal infill panels over bays 18 and 20, a closed brown sectional door with a window strip at 19, thin dark fascia
attached: wall pack between 16 and 17 (z 3.9)
door 19 has a 3-light window strip at z ~1.4
W4.notes: sv_W4_K_8T and sv_W5 (2019/2025): bay pitch ~3.6 m, door 15 next to the W3 canopy end, a block pier after 20 then the stair/fence to the CSB. 6 bays x 3.6 m = 21.6 m of the 27.4 m wall: end widths are a guess. Bays were open with lifts and vehicles inside in all photos.

W5.summary: north end of the west wing, facing the Central Services Building (heating plant) 1-4 m away; not visible in any photo; plain wall with thin dark coping
W5.notes: Guess: W5/W6 continue W4's grey block (they meet at the W4/W5 corner), W7 continues W8's brick. Lidar outside these walls hits the CSB and the stack base (5-27 m), so they are effectively hidden party walls.

geometry_notes: W3 is the edge of the loading canopy, not a wall: the block wall with doors 7-12 stands 2.9 m behind on W2's line (use the undercut). W2 also has the canopy 2.5-2.7 m in front of it at 4.8 m (lidar).
W0 is two volumes: s 0-17.6 brick at 6.9 m (east block), s 17.6-39.1 grey block rising 7.3-7.7 m; W1 (all block) is 7.8 m.

The south face has small recesses the outline skips: between W9 b and W10 a (3.7 m, ~1.5 m deep, contains a grated window and the KEY CONTROL steel door) and between W12 b and W13 a (3.3 m); W11 is set back ~1.9 m from W10/W12. Concrete screen slabs stand in front of the two gaps.
W13: only s ~6-23 is the 8.2 m two-storey block; s 0-6 is 4.7 m (handled with void cells).
W14: the lidar line runs ~2 m in front of the glazing (it includes the canopy); the buff stair tower at s ~4-7.5 rises to 9.1-9.3 m, above the 7.6 m wall.
W5-W7 abut the Central Services Building and its stack; lidar samples near W7's east end (11-27 m) belong to the CSB/stack, not GSC.
East block roof is 6.9-7.0 m along W15-W17 and ~7.7 m at its north end (block part of W0/W1).
